title: Finiteness of the automorphism group of a polarized abelian variety
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $A/k$ be an abelian variety [def-sc-abelian-variety]. Write $A^\vee=\operatorname{Pic}^0_{A/k}$ for the dual abelian variety representing algebraically trivial invertible sheaves rigidified at the identity. Let $\lambda:A\to A^\vee$ be the polarization induced by an ample [def-sc-ample] invertible sheaf [def-sc-invertible-module] $L$, so $\lambda(x)=[t_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}]$, where $t_x$ is translation by $x$. For a $k$-group automorphism $a$ [def-sc-group-scheme], let $a^\vee$ denote pullback on $A^\vee$. Then the group $\operatorname{Aut}_k(A,\lambda)=\{a:A\xrightarrow{\sim}A\text{ a }k\text{-group automorphism}:a^\vee\lambda a=\lambda\}$ is finite.

source.place: Chapter I, Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; polarization convention in I §11, printed p.53.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-abelian-hom-finite-free] with $B=A$. Thus $M=\operatorname{End}_k(A)$ is a free abelian group with a finite integral basis, and its unit is $1=\mathrm{id}_A$. Put $V=M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and write $\iota(m)=m\otimes1$. In the chosen basis $\iota$ is $\mathbf Z^r\hookrightarrow\mathbf Q^r$, so it is injective, including when $r=0$. Composition extends bilinearly to $V$, hence $\iota(mn)=\iota(m)\iota(n)$ and $\iota(1)=1$. We use this injection to regard integral endomorphisms as rational ones in the following steps.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(a), p.62, discreteness input; Theorem 10.15, p.49.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-rosati-trace-positive] to $A,L,\lambda$. Write $\mu=\lambda^{-1}$ in rational homomorphisms. We obtain on $V$ the symmetric positive definite rational bilinear form $B_\lambda(u,v)=\operatorname{Tr}_A(u^\dagger v)$, where $u^\dagger=\mu u^\vee\lambda$, and $\operatorname{Tr}_A(1)=2\dim A$. This uses the given ample polarization, with no principal-polarization assumption.

source.place: §14 p.61 and Theorem 14.3, p.62; Proposition 14.4(a), first paragraph.

proof.text: For $a\in\operatorname{Aut}_k(A,\lambda)$, regard $a$ as $\iota(a)\in V$ using step 1. The defining equation $a^\vee\lambda a=\lambda$ gives $a^\dagger a=\mu a^\vee\lambda a=\mu\lambda=1$. Consequently $B_\lambda(\iota(a),\iota(a))=\operatorname{Tr}_A(1)=2\dim A$. Thus every such $a$, as an element of $M$, belongs to $S=\{m\in M:B_\lambda(\iota(m),\iota(m))\le2\dim A\}$. The products in this calculation are compositions of rational homomorphisms, so no inverse of $\lambda$ in the integral endomorphism ring is asserted.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(a), p.62, calculation of the trace norm.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-positive-form-lattice-sublevels-finite] to $M$, the rational form $B_\lambda$, and $c=2\dim A$. Its finite-basis hypothesis was established in step 1, and symmetry, rational bilinearity and strict positivity on nonzero rational vectors were established in step 2. It follows that $S$ is finite. Forgetting the inverse and the proof of preservation sends $\operatorname{Aut}_k(A,\lambda)$ injectively into $S$: equality of the underlying group-scheme endomorphisms is equality of automorphisms. Thus $\operatorname{Aut}_k(A,\lambda)$ is finite.

source.place: Proposition 14.4(a), p.62, final lattice/compactness inference, with compactness applied to the ellipsoid.

proof_origin.place: Chapter I, Proposition 14.4(a), printed p.62; supporting Theorems 10.15 and 14.3 and Proposition 10.20.

lean.note: Uses the landed normalized dual Poincare datum and rigidified dual-pullback classification. The finite subtype contains exactly the k-group automorphisms satisfying a-dual lambda a=lambda; neither a principal polarization nor an arbitrarily specified dual action is assumed.
